rows.text: The quiz marks VERO. The figure indicates battery charging, not ignition directly. One possible indirect link is an ignition fault that stalls the engine: in a vehicle whose lamp stays on with the ignition on and engine stopped, the lamp may then light. This is an inference from examples involving different vehicles, not a diagnosis; if it stays on with the engine running, check the charging system.
evidence: https://www.hella.com/techworld/en/technical/car-electronics-and-electrics/starting-and-charging-system/checking-the-alternator/ — charging indicator, alternator and electrical faults; no verified direct ignition-fault mechanism.

review.review_evidence: All six distinct quiz images independently inspected. Cited UNECE PDF returned 403; original EU R121 2016/18 PDF URL challenged, but exact 2016 Official Journal publication independently inspected through https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=uriserv%3AOJ.L_.2016.005.01.0009.01.ENG: table includes yellow windscreen tell-tale, fog lamp colours and red charging/coolant symbols. The historical SAE 1943 source supports conditional corrosion consequences, not every modern coolant. Reviewed HELLA Micra/Note ignition-coil stall bulletin and Honda Accord 2002 printed p.326 charging lamp; their combined explanation is explicitly a cross-vehicle conditional inference, not a verified single-vehicle fault.

issues.reason: The printed FALSO rejects even the possibility that exhausted antifreeze can cause the coolant-temperature warning. Sources link depleted corrosion inhibitors to rust, clogged cooling passages and overheating; the question does not specify a direct cause or exclude this indirect pathway. Independent adjudication of the intended scope is needed.
